paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, on one of the days, as he was teaching the people in the temple, and preaching the gospel, there came upon him the chief priests and the scribes with the elders;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν διδάσκοντος αὐτοῦ τὸν λαὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ εὐαγγελιζομένου ἐπέστησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς σὺν τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις,
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto en mia tōn hēmerōn didaskontos autou ton laon en tō hierō kai euangelizomenou epestēsan hoi archiereis kai hoi grammateis syn tois presbyterois,

paragraphs.text: and they spake, saying unto him, Tell us: By what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπαν λέγοντες πρὸς αὐτόν· Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς, ἢ τίς ἐστιν ὁ δούς σοι τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην;
paragraphs.translit: kai eipan legontes pros auton· Eipon hēmin en poia exousia tauta poieis, ē tis estin ho dous soi tēn exousian tautēn;

paragraphs.text: And he answered and said unto them, I also will ask you a question; and tell me:
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς κἀγὼ λόγον, καὶ εἴπατέ μοι·
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de eipen pros autous· Erōtēsō hymas kagō logon, kai eipate moi·

paragraphs.text: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men?
paragraphs.original: Τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἦν ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων;
paragraphs.translit: To baptisma Iōannou ex ouranou ēn ē ex anthrōpōn;

paragraphs.text: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why did ye not believe him?
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ συνελογίσαντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες ὅτι Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ· Διὰ τί οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;
paragraphs.translit: hoi de synelogisanto pros heautous legontes hoti Ean eipōmen· Ex ouranou, erei· Dia ti ouk episteusate autō;

paragraphs.text: But if we shall say, From men; all the people will stone us: for they are persuaded that John was a prophet.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων, ὁ λαὸς ἅπας καταλιθάσει ἡμᾶς, πεπεισμένος γάρ ἐστιν Ἰωάννην προφήτην εἶναι·
paragraphs.translit: ean de eipōmen· Ex anthrōpōn, ho laos hapas katalithasei hēmas, pepeismenos gar estin Iōannēn prophētēn einai·

paragraphs.text: And they answered, that they knew not whence [it was].
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν μὴ εἰδέναι πόθεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apekrithēsan mē eidenai pothen.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho Iēsous eipen autois· Oude egō legō hymin en poia exousia tauta poiō.

paragraphs.text: And he began to speak unto the people this parable: A man planted a vineyard, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into another country for a long time.
paragraphs.original: Ἤρξατο δὲ πρὸς τὸν λαὸν λέγειν τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην· Ἄνθρωπος ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα, καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν χρόνους ἱκανούς.
paragraphs.translit: Ērxato de pros ton laon legein tēn parabolēn tautēn· Anthrōpos ephyteusen ampelōna, kai exedeto auton geōrgois, kai apedēmēsen chronous hikanous.

paragraphs.text: And at the season he sent unto the husbandmen a servant, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard: but the husbandmen beat him, and sent him away empty.
paragraphs.original: καὶ καιρῷ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς δοῦλον, ἵνα ἀπὸ τοῦ καρποῦ τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος δώσουσιν αὐτῷ· οἱ δὲ γεωργοὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν αὐτὸν δείραντες κενόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai kairō apesteilen pros tous geōrgous doulon, hina apo tou karpou tou ampelōnos dōsousin autō· hoi de geōrgoi exapesteilan auton deirantes kenon.

paragraphs.text: And he sent yet another servant: and him also they beat, and handled him shamefully, and sent him away empty.
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσέθετο ἕτερον πέμψαι δοῦλον· οἱ δὲ κἀκεῖνον δείραντες καὶ ἀτιμάσαντες ἐξαπέστειλαν κενόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai prosetheto heteron pempsai doulon· hoi de kakeinon deirantes kai atimasantes exapesteilan kenon.

paragraphs.text: And he sent yet a third: and him also they wounded, and cast him forth.
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσέθετο τρίτον πέμψαι· οἱ δὲ καὶ τοῦτον τραυματίσαντες ἐξέβαλον.
paragraphs.translit: kai prosetheto triton pempsai· hoi de kai touton traumatisantes exebalon.

paragraphs.text: And the lord of the vineyard said, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; it may be they will reverence him.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος· Τί ποιήσω; πέμψω τὸν υἱόν μου τὸν ἀγαπητόν· ἴσως τοῦτον ἐντραπήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de ho kyrios tou ampelōnos· Ti poiēsō; pempsō ton hyion mou ton agapēton· isōs touton entrapēsontai.

paragraphs.text: But when the husbandmen saw him, they reasoned one with another, saying, This is the heir; let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.
paragraphs.original: ἰδόντες δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ γεωργοὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος· ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν, ἵνα ἡμῶν γένηται ἡ κληρονομία·
paragraphs.translit: idontes de auton hoi geōrgoi dielogizonto pros allēlous legontes· Houtos estin ho klēronomos· apokteinōmen auton, hina hēmōn genētai hē klēronomia·

paragraphs.text: And they cast him forth out of the vineyard, and killed him. What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do unto them?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐκβαλόντες αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος ἀπέκτειναν. τί οὖν ποιήσει αὐτοῖς ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος;
paragraphs.translit: kai ekbalontes auton exō tou ampelōnos apekteinan. ti oun poiēsei autois ho kyrios tou ampelōnos;

paragraphs.text: He will come and destroy these husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others. And when they heard it, they said, God forbid.
paragraphs.original: ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀπολέσει τοὺς γεωργοὺς τούτους, καὶ δώσει τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἄλλοις. ἀκούσαντες δὲ εἶπαν· Μὴ γένοιτο.
paragraphs.translit: eleusetai kai apolesei tous geōrgous toutous, kai dōsei ton ampelōna allois. akousantes de eipan· Mē genoito.

paragraphs.text: But he looked upon them, and said, What then is this that is written, The stone which the builders rejected, The same was made the head of the corner?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς εἶπεν· Τί οὖν ἐστιν τὸ γεγραμμένον τοῦτο· Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες, οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας;
paragraphs.translit: ho de emblepsas autois eipen· Ti oun estin to gegrammenon touto· Lithon hon apedokimasan hoi oikodomountes, houtos egenēthē eis kephalēn gōnias;

paragraphs.text: Every one that falleth on that stone shall be broken to pieces; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will scatter him as dust.
paragraphs.original: πᾶς ὁ πεσὼν ἐπʼ ἐκεῖνον τὸν λίθον συνθλασθήσεται· ἐφʼ ὃν δʼ ἂν πέσῃ, λικμήσει αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: pas ho pesōn epʼ ekeinon ton lithon synthlasthēsetai· ephʼ hon dʼ an pesē, likmēsei auton.

paragraphs.text: And the scribes and the chief priests sought to lay hands on him in that very hour; and they feared the people: for they perceived that he spake this parable against them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐζήτησαν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐπιβαλεῖν ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸν λαόν, ἔγνωσαν γὰρ ὅτι πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην.
paragraphs.translit: kai ezētēsan hoi grammateis kai hoi archiereis epibalein epʼ auton tas cheiras en autē tē hōra, kai ephobēthēsan ton laon, egnōsan gar hoti pros autous eipen tēn parabolēn tautēn.

paragraphs.text: And they watched him, and sent forth spies, who feigned themselves to be righteous, that they might take hold of his speech, so as to deliver him up to the rule and to the authority of the governor.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ παρατηρήσαντες ἀπέστειλαν ἐγκαθέτους ὑποκρινομένους ἑαυτοὺς δικαίους εἶναι, ἵνα ἐπιλάβωνται αὐτοῦ λόγου, ὥστε παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν τῇ ἀρχῇ καὶ τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος.
paragraphs.translit: Kai paratērēsantes apesteilan enkathetous hypokrinomenous heautous dikaious einai, hina epilabōntai autou logou, hōste paradounai auton tē archē kai tē exousia tou hēgemonos.

paragraphs.text: And they asked him, saying, Teacher, we know that thou sayest and teachest rightly, and acceptest not the person [of any], but of a truth teachest the way of God:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ὀρθῶς λέγεις καὶ διδάσκεις καὶ οὐ λαμβάνεις πρόσωπον, ἀλλʼ ἐπʼ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ διδάσκεις·
paragraphs.translit: kai epērōtēsan auton legontes· Didaskale, oidamen hoti orthōs legeis kai didaskeis kai ou lambaneis prosōpon, allʼ epʼ alētheias tēn hodon tou theou didaskeis·

paragraphs.text: Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?
paragraphs.original: ἔξεστιν ἡμᾶς Καίσαρι φόρον δοῦναι ἢ οὔ;
paragraphs.translit: exestin hēmas Kaisari phoron dounai ē ou;

paragraphs.text: But he perceived their craftiness, and said unto them,
paragraphs.original: κατανοήσας δὲ αὐτῶν τὴν πανουργίαν εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς·
paragraphs.translit: katanoēsas de autōn tēn panourgian eipen pros autous·

paragraphs.text: Show me a denarius. Whose image and superscription hath it? And they said, Caesar`s.
paragraphs.original: Δείξατέ μοι δηνάριον· τίνος ἔχει εἰκόνα καὶ ἐπιγραφήν; ἀποκριθέντες δὲ εἶπαν· Καίσαρος.
paragraphs.translit: Deixate moi dēnarion· tinos echei eikona kai epigraphēn; apokrithentes de eipan· Kaisaros.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Then render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar`s, and unto God the things that are God`s.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τοίνυν ἀπόδοτε τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen pros autous· Toinyn apodote ta Kaisaros Kaisari kai ta tou theou tō theō.

paragraphs.text: And they were not able to take hold of the saying before the people: and they marvelled at his answer, and held their peace.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν ἐπιλαβέσθαι τοῦ ῥήματος ἐναντίον τοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ θαυμάσαντες ἐπὶ τῇ ἀποκρίσει αὐτοῦ ἐσίγησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk ischysan epilabesthai tou rhēmatos enantion tou laou, kai thaumasantes epi tē apokrisei autou esigēsan.

paragraphs.text: And there came to him certain of the Sadducees, they that say that there is no resurrection;
paragraphs.original: Προσελθόντες δέ τινες τῶν Σαδδουκαίων, οἱ ἀντιλέγοντες ἀνάστασιν μὴ εἶναι, ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν
paragraphs.translit: Proselthontes de tines tōn Saddoukaiōn, hoi antilegontes anastasin mē einai, epērōtēsan auton

paragraphs.text: and they asked him, saying, Teacher, Moses wrote unto us, that if a man`s brother die, having a wife, and he be childless, his brother should take the wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
paragraphs.original: λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν, ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ ἔχων γυναῖκα, καὶ οὗτος ἄτεκνος ᾖ, ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: legontes· Didaskale, Mōysēs egrapsen hēmin, ean tinos adelphos apothanē echōn gynaika, kai houtos ateknos ē, hina labē ho adelphos autou tēn gynaika kai exanastēsē sperma tō adelphō autou.

paragraphs.text: There were therefore seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and died childless;
paragraphs.original: ἑπτὰ οὖν ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος λαβὼν γυναῖκα ἀπέθανεν ἄτεκνος·
paragraphs.translit: hepta oun adelphoi ēsan· kai ho prōtos labōn gynaika apethanen ateknos·

paragraphs.text: and the second:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ δεύτερος
paragraphs.translit: kai ho deuteros

paragraphs.text: and the third took her; and likewise the seven also left no children, and died.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἔλαβεν αὐτήν, ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ οὐ κατέλιπον τέκνα καὶ ἀπέθανον·
paragraphs.translit: kai ho tritos elaben autēn, hōsautōs de kai hoi hepta ou katelipon tekna kai apethanon·

paragraphs.text: Afterward the woman also died.
paragraphs.original: ὕστερον καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν.
paragraphs.translit: hysteron kai hē gynē apethanen.

paragraphs.text: In the resurrection therefore whose wife of them shall she be? for the seven had her to wife.
paragraphs.original: ἡ γυνὴ οὖν ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τίνος αὐτῶν γίνεται γυνή; οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα.
paragraphs.translit: hē gynē oun en tē anastasei tinos autōn ginetai gynē; hoi gar hepta eschon autēn gynaika.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto them, The sons of this world marry, and are given in marriage:
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου γαμοῦσιν καὶ γαμίσκονται,
paragraphs.translit: Kai eipen autois ho Iēsous· Hoi hyioi tou aiōnos toutou gamousin kai gamiskontai,

paragraphs.text: but they that are accounted worthy to attain to that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage:
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ καταξιωθέντες τοῦ αἰῶνος ἐκείνου τυχεῖν καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῆς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται·
paragraphs.translit: hoi de kataxiōthentes tou aiōnos ekeinou tychein kai tēs anastaseōs tēs ek nekrōn oute gamousin oute gamizontai·

paragraphs.text: for neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
paragraphs.original: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἀποθανεῖν ἔτι δύνανται, ἰσάγγελοι γάρ εἰσιν καὶ υἱοί εἰσιν θεοῦ τῆς ἀναστάσεως υἱοὶ ὄντες.
paragraphs.translit: oude gar apothanein eti dynantai, isangeloi gar eisin kai hyioi eisin theou tēs anastaseōs hyioi ontes.

paragraphs.text: But that the dead are raised, even Moses showed, in [the place concerning] the Bush, when he calleth the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι δὲ ἐγείρονται οἱ νεκροὶ καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἐμήνυσεν ἐπὶ τῆς βάτου, ὡς λέγει κύριον τὸν θεὸν Ἀβραὰμ καὶ θεὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ θεὸν Ἰακώβ·
paragraphs.translit: hoti de egeirontai hoi nekroi kai Mōysēs emēnysen epi tēs batou, hōs legei kyrion ton theon Abraam kai theon Isaak kai theon Iakōb·

paragraphs.text: Now he is not the God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.
paragraphs.original: θεὸς δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων, πάντες γὰρ αὐτῷ ζῶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: theos de ouk estin nekrōn alla zōntōn, pantes gar autō zōsin.

paragraphs.text: And certain of the scribes answering said, Teacher, thou hast well said.
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθέντες δέ τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν· Διδάσκαλε, καλῶς εἶπας·
paragraphs.translit: apokrithentes de tines tōn grammateōn eipan· Didaskale, kalōs eipas·

paragraphs.text: For they durst not any more ask him any question.
paragraphs.original: οὐκέτι γὰρ ἐτόλμων ἐπερωτᾶν αὐτὸν οὐδέν.
paragraphs.translit: ouketi gar etolmōn eperōtan auton ouden.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, How say they that the Christ is David`s son?
paragraphs.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Πῶς λέγουσιν τὸν χριστὸν εἶναι Δαυὶδ υἱόν;
paragraphs.translit: Eipen de pros autous· Pōs legousin ton christon einai Dauid hyion;

paragraphs.text: For David himself saith in the book of Psalms, The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand,
paragraphs.original: αὐτὸς γὰρ Δαυὶδ λέγει ἐν βίβλῳ ψαλμῶν· Εἶπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου
paragraphs.translit: autos gar Dauid legei en biblō psalmōn· Eipen kyrios tō kyriō mou· Kathou ek dexiōn mou

paragraphs.text: Till I make thine enemies the footstool of thy feet.
paragraphs.original: ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.
paragraphs.translit: heōs an thō tous echthrous sou hypopodion tōn podōn sou.

paragraphs.text: David therefore calleth him Lord, and how is he his son?
paragraphs.original: Δαυὶδ οὖν αὐτὸν κύριον καλεῖ, καὶ πῶς αὐτοῦ υἱός ἐστιν;
paragraphs.translit: Dauid oun auton kyrion kalei, kai pōs autou hyios estin;

paragraphs.text: And in the hearing of all the people he said unto his disciples,
paragraphs.original: Ἀκούοντος δὲ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς·
paragraphs.translit: Akouontos de pantos tou laou eipen tois mathētais·

paragraphs.text: Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk in long robes, and love salutations in the marketplaces, and chief seats in the synagogues, and chief places at feasts;
paragraphs.original: Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν γραμματέων τῶν θελόντων περιπατεῖν ἐν στολαῖς καὶ φιλούντων ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ πρωτοκλισίας ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις,
paragraphs.translit: Prosechete apo tōn grammateōn tōn thelontōn peripatein en stolais kai philountōn aspasmous en tais agorais kai prōtokathedrias en tais synagōgais kai prōtoklisias en tois deipnois,

paragraphs.text: who devour widows` houses, and for a pretence make long prayers: these shall receive greater condemnation.
paragraphs.original: οἳ κατεσθίουσιν τὰς οἰκίας τῶν χηρῶν καὶ προφάσει μακρὰ προσεύχονται· οὗτοι λήμψονται περισσότερον κρίμα.
paragraphs.translit: hoi katesthiousin tas oikias tōn chērōn kai prophasei makra proseuchontai· houtoi lēmpsontai perissoteron krima.
